worksheet.title: Run It Top to Bottom
worksheet.subtitle: Blocks run in order, from the top down
worksheet.learning_goal: I can tell the order the blocks in a stack run.

parts.title: Top to bottom
parts.text: Bit runs a stack from the TOP block down. The top block runs first. Then the next block. Then the next — one block at a time, all the way to the bottom.

parts.title: Bit's stack
parts.note: Bit runs the top ⚑ block first, then works down: ➡, then ⬆, then ⬅ at the bottom.

parts.title: Runs first
parts.prompt: Circle the block Bit runs FIRST. Remember: Bit always starts at the top.

parts.title: Number the order
parts.prompt: Bit runs the stack from top to bottom. Write 1, 2, 3, 4 on the blocks above to show the order Bit runs them. The top ⚑ block is 1.

parts.title: You try
parts.prompt: Look at the new stack. Circle the block Bit runs LAST (the bottom one). Then write 1, 2, 3 on the blocks to show the run order.

parts.title: Big idea
parts.text: A program runs in order, from the top down, one block at a time. The order of the blocks is the algorithm — change the order and Bit does something different.

teacher_guide.eyebrow: Teacher Guide · Kindergarten · Intro Block Coding
teacher_guide.title: Run It Top to Bottom
teacher_guide.subtitle: Quick facilitation notes & answer key
teacher_guide.footer_topic: 2. Run It Top to Bottom — Teacher Guide

parts.title: Goal
parts.text: Children learn that a block program runs from the top block down, one block at a time, and that the position of a block decides when it runs. This builds the core idea of sequential execution: the order of the blocks IS the algorithm.

parts.title: Kindergarten frame (Ontario)
text: Problem Solving and Innovating — children determine and describe the order in which a set of instructions is carried out.
No reading required of the child: read each prompt aloud; the child circles a block and writes order numbers (1-4).

parts.title: Materials
parts.text: The printed worksheet and a pencil. Optional: the 4 paper blocks from Sheet 1 plus an up ⬆ and left ⬅ block to physically point to in order.

parts.title: Run it (about 15 min)
text: 1. MODEL: point to Bit's stack and tap each block in turn — '⚑ runs first… ➡ second… ⬆ third… ⬅ last.' One tap per block, top to bottom.
2. GUIDED: Exercise 1 — circle the top ⚑ block (runs first). Exercise 2 — children write 1, 2, 3, 4 down the stack.
3. YOU TRY: Exercise 3 — on the second stack, circle the bottom ➡ (runs last) and number 1, 2, 3.
4. Connect: 'A computer runs its blocks in order, top to bottom — it never skips around.'

parts.title: Answer key (modelled by the run-gate)
text: Ex 1 — Bit runs the top ⚑ GO block first.
Ex 3 — the last block is the bottom ➡; order down the second stack: ⚑ = 1, ⬅ = 2, ➡ = 3.

parts.title: Watch for & differentiate
text: Common slip: numbering bottom-to-top. Re-anchor: 'We always start at the TOP, like reading starts at the top of the page.'
Simplify: cover all blocks but the top, reveal one at a time as you count.
Extend: ask 'if we swapped the ➡ and the ⬅, would Bit do the same thing?' (No — order matters.)
Movement option: stand 4 children in a line holding blocks; tap shoulders top-to-bottom so each acts in turn.

parts.title: Success looks like
parts.text: The child numbers the blocks 1, 2, 3, 4 from the top down and names the first and last blocks correctly for both stacks.
